dedupe_keys.name: nordic fire statistics fire deaths 2010 to 2024 and building fires 2016 to 2024 for denmark estonia finland iceland norway and sweden

description: Nordic Fire Statistics is a joint effort by the fire authorities of Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Iceland, Norway and Sweden to publish fire deaths and building fires on shared definitions, so that the fire problem can be compared across countries. It is hosted by the Swedish civil defence agency MCF. A fire death is counted when the national fire authority judges that a person died within 30 days from injuries sustained in a fire. Four spreadsheets give fire deaths per year from 2010 to 2024 and building fires per year from 2016 to 2024, each also expressed per million population, with one row per country. The files are free and available to download from the page, which also links to each country's national fire statistics service. Caveats: the site is being revised and currently shows only basic recent series, Iceland has no values after 2021, and counts are national totals without causes or locations. Simulation uses: benchmarking national fire risk and rescue service outcomes, calibrating residential fire frequency in building and emergency service models, and comparing trends across similar systems. Related records: the Swedish rescue service statistics (data-mcf-sweden-rescue-service-statistics) give municipal detail for one member, and the CTIF world fire statistics (data-ctif-world-fire-statistics) give a wider international comparison.
